Heard learned counsel for the rival parties.
3. This is first bail application filed by the applicants under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

The applicants are in apprehension of their arrest in connection with Crime No.

sentences.text: 4. The allegation against the applicants and other co-accused persons is that they were involved in the aforesaid case and had executed a sale deed of a land to the complainant Pragya Mishra which was subsequently found to be of government lease.

It is alleged that the government land has been sold by the applicants and other co-accused persons to the complainant for a consideration amount of Rs. 21,15,000/- and she has been duped of the said amount.
On the basis of the aforesaid, crime has been registered.
5 . Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants are falsely implicated in the matter.
As per the version of the FIR, it is stated that the complainant had transferred the amount to Sachin and Jagdish.
In fact the present applicants have not received any consideration amount for the sale of the said land.
The applicants have no criminal antecedents.
He further submits that the co-accused Kamna Rathore, Maya Bai, Madhu Bai, Seema Bai and Mamta Bai have been granted anticipatory by this Court.
Hence, the applicants be also granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application by contending that on the basis of the allegations and material evidence available on record no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
Investigation is going on.
Custodial interrogation may be required.
In the aforesaid circumstances, the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.
7. However, it would not be desirable to enter into the merits of the rival contentions at this juncture.

8. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, looking to the gravity of the offence and the role assigned to the present applicants in the crime, I am of the view that no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
9. Consequently, the first application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicants stands rejected.
10. Certified copy as per rules.
